terms.comment: A plain place: locum quaerimus, we’re looking for a space; locus vacuus, a free one. To park is autoraedam statuere, and the car park ārea statīva (Traupman 217).

sources: Lewis & Short: locus · Lewis & Short: vacuus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 217, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
